Invoice basics

Everything a new business owner should know before creating an invoice

What should a contractor invoice include?

A contractor invoice should include business details, customer details, project or site reference, labor, material, quantity, rate, tax, total and payment terms.

How to bill milestones

Use separate line items for advance payment, stage completion, material delivery, labor completion or final handover.

Labor and material breakdown

Separating labor and materials helps customers understand the charge and reduces back-and-forth before payment.

PDF invoice sharing

PDF invoices are easier to share on WhatsApp or email and look more reliable than screenshots.

Practical tips

Invoice details that help clients pay faster

Separate labor and material charges when the customer needs a clear breakdown.
Mention project name, site name or milestone in the invoice description.
Add due date and payment terms before sending the bill.
Use tax fields when GST or other tax applies to the contractor work.
Keep invoice numbers consistent across jobs and customers.
